name: Losartan + Hydrochlorothiazide
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start losartan/HCTZ 50/12.5 mg once daily; increase after about 3 weeks to a maximum of 100/25 mg once daily

usual_adult_dose.indication: Hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy (not controlled on monotherapy)
usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 50/12.5 mg; titrate to a maximum of 100/25 mg

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Potassium-raising drugs (potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, salt substitutes)

key_interactions.effect: Higher lithium levels and toxicity (ARBs and thiazides).
Worse kidney function, possible acute renal failure (older, volume-depleted or CKD patients); weaker antihypertensive and diuretic effect.
key_interactions.action: Monitor kidney function periodically; check that blood pressure and diuretic effect are maintained.

key_interactions.effect: Dual RAS blockade: hypotension, hyperkalemia, kidney function changes.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: ACE inhibitors, other ARBs, aliskiren (dual RAS blockade)
key_interactions.effect: More hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia and acute renal failure without added benefit in most patients.
key_interactions.action: Avoid routine combination; monitor blood pressure, kidney function and electrolytes if used.
Antidiabetic dose adjustment may be needed.
Label states the effect only; no interval given.

common: Dizziness, upper respiratory infection, cough, back pain (≥2% and more than placebo)
serious: Hypotension in volume- or salt-depleted patients
Acute kidney function changes, including acute renal failure
Electrolyte and metabolic effects (hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, hyperuricemia, glucose changes)
Acute myopia and secondary angle-closure glaucoma (HCTZ)
Nonmelanoma skin cancer, mainly squamous cell carcinoma with large cumulative HCTZ doses (postmarketing)

contraindications: Coadministration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes
monitoring: Serum potassium, sodium and creatinine periodically
Stop at once if pregnancy is detected

pk.peak: Losartan 1 hour; active metabolite 3 to 4 hours
pk.half_life: Losartan about 2 hours; metabolite 6 to 9 hours; HCTZ 5.6 to 14.8 hours
pk.half_life_eskd: Not reported. Losartan AUC 50% to 90% higher at CrCl 30 to 74; HCTZ AUC 70% (mild) to 700% (moderate) higher (label)
pk.vd: Losartan about 34 L; active metabolite about 12 L
pk.metabolism: Losartan: CYP2C9 and CYP3A4; about 14% converted to the active carboxylic acid metabolite. HCTZ: not metabolized
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Losartan about 4% unchanged and 6% as metabolite in urine; HCTZ at least 61% unchanged in urine within 24 hours
pk.dialyzability: Losartan and metabolite: no. HCTZ: not established (label).

sources.citation: Organon LLC. (2025). HYZAAR (losartan potassium and hydrochlorothiazide) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA020387, set ID 4116ccde-2e23-45f4-b12f-6337df877744, version effective November 26, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: Electrolyte list in ae_serious condenses label 5.5; confirm wording.
Nonmelanoma skin cancer comes from the postmarketing part of Adverse Reactions, not a numbered warning in this label version.
Dual RAS blockade row (Avoid) is our severity call; the label states the risks without the word 'avoid' except aliskiren in diabetes (contraindicated).
